doc.title: Mark Soskin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 17, 2021

title: Today's jazz students
summary: Students in his Rollins band play very well and he encourages them, unlike his own teachers.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Anything surprise you about the current jazz students that you didn’t expect?

You know what? They’re playing their butts off. I mean they’re really, I mean this group that I have with Sonny Rollins, man, I mean the level that they’re, there’s two tenor players in this band, piano, bass and drums. They’re all playing so well and I tell them that. They’re really — I mean when I was that age I don’t know if I was playing that well. You know? The way they — whatever they’re doing they’re doing something right because, and when they get into the real world they’re going to be ready. And I try to encourage that. I didn’t have teachers who were like that. I didn’t have teachers that encouraged me. They just said do what you do. You know, whatever. But I tell my students, especially this band, that they’re great. I don’t want them to get big heads but they’re doing something right and it should be encouraged.
